policy_title: Improve Maternity Care and Healthcare Management
stated: Labour will ensure trusts failing on maternity care are robustly supported, train thousands more midwives, and set an explicit target to close the Black and Asian maternal mortality gap. They will digitise the Red Book record of children’s health and enable vaccinations for babies and children during health visits. The party will implement professional standards and regulate NHS managers, establish a Royal College of Clinical Leadership, and work to implement Cass Review recommendations for young people with gender dysphoria.

source.quote: Childbirth should not be something women fear or look back on with trauma. Labour will ensure that trusts failing on maternity care are robustly supported into rapid improvement. We will train thousands more midwives as part of the NHS Workforce Plan and set an explicit target to close the Black and Asian maternal mortality gap. Labour will digitise the Red Book record of children’s health, improving support for new families. We will also enable vaccinations for babies and children as part of health visits. Labour will implement professional standards and regulate NHS managers, ensuring those who commit serious misconduct can never do so again. And we will establish a Royal College of Clinical Leadership to champion the voice of clinicians. We will work to implement the expert recommendations of the Cass Review to ensure that young people presenting to the NHS with gender dysphoria are receiving appropriate and high-quality care.

bearing_set.reason: Training more midwives, supporting failing maternity trusts, digitising child health records, enabling health-visit vaccinations, and regulating NHS managers all directly affect healthcare access, capacity, and quality of care.

Setting an explicit government target to close the Black and Asian maternal mortality gap is a direct equal-treatment/anti-discrimination measure for a minority group; implementing Cass Review recommendations has significant implications for the treatment of gender-diverse young people as a minority in healthcare.

Implementing Cass Review recommendations restricts access to puberty blockers and gender-affirming hormone treatments for young trans people through the NHS, constituting a state-mediated constraint on bodily autonomy for that group — a concrete O10 bodily-autonomy mechanism.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: O3 is the primary target; O9 is engaged by the racial mortality-gap pledge specifically; O10 is engaged by the Cass Review implementation, which materially restricts treatment options for a specific group on bodily-autonomy grounds.
